parts.note: Angle DAB = 180 - 116 = 64 (co-interior, AD parallel to BC); bisected gives 32; both give 32 degrees.

parts.label: (b)
parts.note: Angle DEA = angle EAB = 32 (alternate, DC parallel to AB), so angle AEC = 180 - 32 = 148 (straight line DEC); both give 148 degrees. Figure checked: with A(0,0), B(9,0), D(2.19,4.49), E(7.19,4.49) the angle at A is 64.0, at B 116, AD = DE = 5 so AE really is the bisector and E is strictly between D and C.

key_verdict: No disagreement; the setter's key is correct in both parts and the described figure is consistent with the data.
why: A plane-geometry angle chase in the exact 4052 P1 register (short givens, 'Find angle ...', 1 + 2 marks matching one step then two steps), with a clean 116-degree datum and a figure that shows only the given angle; the point-on-a-side device is shared with 2025 P1 Q13 but the shape (parallelogram), the mechanism (bisector plus parallel lines) and the target angles are different, so it is not a re-skin.
